title: One Gate Scheme to Rule Them All: Introducing a Complex Yet Reduced Instruction Set for Quantum Computing
problem: Designing an efficient quantum instruction set for qubits with XX+YY coupling that can realize any two-qubit gate with high fidelity while achieving minimal gate counts.
motivation: Quantum instruction set architecture directly impacts quantum computer performance and the practical feasibility of executing quantum algorithms with high fidelity.
method: The work introduces a set of quantum operations (called CRISC—a compact yet comprehensive quantum instruction set) for qubits connected by XX+YY coupling (a specific type of interaction between qubits). These operations can create any possible two-qubit gate by combining single-qubit operations. The scheme manages decoherence—the gradual loss of quantum information over time—to maintain high accuracy while simultaneously minimizing the number of operations needed to run quantum algorithms.
key_novelty: The scheme achieves the seemingly contradictory goal of a minimal yet complete instruction set by exploiting fundamental differences between quantum and classical computer architectures.
contributions: Gate scheme for XX+YY coupled qubits enabling direct realization of any two-qubit gate
High-fidelity execution framework addressing decoherence as the primary error source
Complete SU(4) group coverage yielding optimal two-qubit gate counts
CRISC architecture combining compactness with comprehensive quantum operation support
limitations: Specific experimental results and comparison baselines not discussed in abstract.
